name: Identify common birds in your area
blurb: Twenty local species covers almost everything you will see in a garden or park. Learning them turns background noise into information.
gear: A regional bird guide or app
A notebook or a birding app for records
steps: Learn the ten most common species where you live first — they account for most sightings and give you a size and shape baseline.
Learn to identify by GISS: general size, shape, behaviour and habitat, rather than by plumage detail.
Learn the calls of five species. Sound identifies far more birds than sight does, especially in woodland.
Keep a list with date, place and what the bird was doing.
Visit the same patch weekly through a season to see how the population changes.
Use a sound-identification app to check yourself, but guess before you look.
tips: Behaviour is often more diagnostic than colour — how it flies, where it feeds, whether it bobs.
Juveniles and winter plumage confuse everyone. Do not assume you have found a rarity.
proof: You identify 20 local species by sight and five by call, unaided.
